Enemies

127 object types, each with hit points, attack, a death type and a tile block of its own art; 47 spawn scripts that the labyrinth's rooms name; and a loader that decompresses enemy art into CHR RAM as rooms are entered.

How a fight is decided

An object lives in one of 24 slots, its fields at $0500 + $18 × field + slot. $0500 is the type; bank 6 dispatches behaviour on it, and bit 7 is set once $CFA0 has filled four fields from the per-type tables. Slots 0-4 are the player's side: $D348 tests only those against everything else, skipping any whose $0578 has bit 7 set and requiring the collision class the caller names. $D364 overlaps two boxes, each the position ± a half-size looked up by metasprite id in $C174/$C201. On a hit $D30E subtracts each side's attack ($05A8) from the other's hit points ($0590), clamping at 0, and at 0 $D32A turns the object into its death type. The player is treated differently: the damage is divided by the player's own $0590 first.

How the corridor bosses move and fire

There is no shared boss engine: the boss type for a corridor comes from bank 3 $9151, and each type's behaviour is its own state machine in bank 6, built from a few shared routines. Whether a boss follows the player is therefore a property of each handler.

Read from the code, not observed. Only Fleepa's setup values are checked against a savestate (target y $10, mask $0F, and a y and velocity matching the bounce its code implies). Direction numbers are 0-15 in 22.5° steps; 0/4/8/12 are right/down/left/up (corrected: this said down/right/up/left; the routine that turns a direction into a velocity was run and the player's own upward shot is 12).

Corridor 21 never reads bank 3 $9151: bank 4's command 5 carries the boss type ($E7AF), and its stream names six in turn - Fleepa, Zibzub, Clawbot ($25), Optomon ($2F), Grimgrin ($48) and Bombarder ($4D) - a boss gauntlet. After it the game plays a short scene ($ECC7 far-calls bank 0) and does INC $51 into corridor 22, whose slot in $9151 is $4F: It, the final boss, in a short corridor of its own (bank 4 stream $8511, 11 records). Corridors 0, 7 and 17 name type $06, the stage bosses (see the next section). The shared shot, type $27 ($A0C6), can turn toward the player when its $07A0 timer reaches zero; which bosses' shots do so is not worked out, so “aimed” means the direction at the moment of firing. Non-boss enemies have not been read.

Bosses that are part of the stage

Corridors 0, 7 and 17 list type $06 as their boss (bank 3 $9151), and type $06 is not something you can see. Its handler, bank 6 $A889, waits until the scroll has stopped, counts the objects of types $36, $37, $7E and $7F still alive and dies when there are none - which is what ends the fight. Those are ground objects, spawned by the stage’s own background tiles (bank 5 $89FB) and drawn over them, so the boss is a part of the scenery. The names are the owner’s (see Outside sources).

Run, not recorded. These frames come from tools/render-bosses.py, which runs the ROM’s own code on the NES model in tools/tgl/cpu.py (no cycle accuracy, no IRQ, one scroll value per scanline from the logged writes) from a corridor savestate, loading each corridor with $EC94 and keeping the ship’s life and lives topped up. The ship is usually destroyed by then, which leaves the boss alone on screen. The layouts are the code’s; exact colours and pixels are the model’s and have not been compared with hardware.

When an enemy leaves an item box

It is not luck. Every enemy killed adds a weight to one counter, and a box is released each time the counter reaches the next step of a fixed schedule. The contents are fixed by the step too. Bank 1 $8176 does it, called from the explosion handler (bank 6 $975F) on the first frame of a type-$08 explosion.

The rules

  1. An enemy whose death type ($D441) is $08 becomes that explosion; 77 types do, and all but five of them have a weight, so they are the ones that can count. Types that die into $07 (bosses such as $45 and $46) never do.
  2. The dead type's weight comes from $823D[type], 0 meaning it does not count. The counter $43 goes up one at a time, up to that weight, and stops the moment it equals the current step's threshold ($8219[$42]); any weight left over is lost.
  3. At the threshold the explosion turns into a box ($0788 set). In the labyrinth the box needs a free cell: $8006 reads the room's cell map ($0400) at the grid-snapped position and $822D[cell] says whether it may; if not, the counter is put back one so the next kill tries again. In a corridor there is no check.
  4. The box takes the next step's contents, $42 goes up by one, and after step 7 (or when the counter wraps past 255) $42 and $43 restart. $42-$44 are cleared only when a game begins, so the schedule carries on from room to room and corridor to corridor.

The schedule (weighted kills, then contents)

BoxCounter reachesContents

8256rotates by $44 through $15, $0C, $0C, $0B: +500 chips and +16 life; life filled to its maximum; life filled to its maximum; +16 life, +20 Enemy Eraser uses and the Eraser counted as owned (only offered when it already is), or $0C when the Eraser is not owned

So a box comes after 50, 80, 100, 140, 180, 220, 230 and 256 weighted kills, and the cycle repeats every 256: boxes at 306, 336, 356, …. Each pickup is applied by bank 2 $86BC; the values $0B-$0C are the labyrinth item icons of the same numbers (weapon 12 and the Energy Tank), and $14-$16 exist only as box contents.

Assembled from the ROM, and checked. Each picture is a metasprite the type's behaviour code assigns (bank 6, and the banks its far calls reach, through $0548), drawn the way $CC46/$CDD7 draw it: 8×16 sprites, each the tile pair t AND $FE and the next, relative to the base tile where the type's block was loaded; mirrored records drawn twice; flips by attribute bits 6 and 7. Colours are bank 5 $B30A records 0-3, which is exactly what sprite palette RAM holds in both savestates. 135 of 146 type/metasprite pairs shown use only even tiles inside the type's own block. The rest either reach into the block its load stream packs next (bosses; drawn from that run) or were attributed through a subroutine several handlers share (dashed outlines mark tiles the run does not reach). Against hardware: parse-metasprites.py --verify predicts every live object's sprites from RAM and finds each multi-sprite shape drawn that frame whole in the in-game savestate's OAM — tiles, placement and attributes.
Not established. Which type is which enemy by name; what each $0620 drawing flag (from $D1A9) does; the meaning of the individual flag bits beyond bit 7 and the collision classes. Types $76-$7F have no art entry: $CFC4 ends at type $75, and a lookup past it would read the flags table.

Spawn scripts

A labyrinth room with byte 1 bit 3 set names a script ($57); $A480 finds it through $A4C7 and bank 7 $F78F runs it a step at a time. formation type × count / interval creates a type-$29 spawner (bank 6 $9A19) that makes count of the type, one every interval frames; wait is in units of 60 frames. All 47 are used by the map.

Five scripts do not end cleanly — run, not just read. Ids 16, 24, 28, 32 and 38 (28 rooms) finish [byte] 01 02. The byte after a formation is always read as its delay, so [byte] is not a spawn (though it equals a type other scripts spawn singly: $70, $54, $73): it is a wait of 112, 112, 84, 115 and 30 seconds in the labyrinth. Then command 1 jumps to (02, the next script's first byte): $6F02, $7202, $9002, $F002, $6502. Running the interpreter on the NES model: scripts 28 and 32 jump into ROM (bank 5 map data, fixed-bank code) and read it as script, spawning a stream of junk formations and objects from then on; scripts 16, 24 and 38 jump into $6000-$7FFF, where this cartridge has nothing. A console returns open bus there; if that is the pointer's high byte (what the 6502 fetched last) the interpreter spawns that type — $6F, $72, $65 — once per wait, for ever. Lead: the open-bus value is an inference, and nothing here is checked on hardware. tools/run-spawn-script.py reproduces it.

The corridors

Enemies in the 21 vertically corridors come from two places. Waves: bank 4's screen-data command 2, with bit 1 of its operand set ($E733), points $66/$67 at a spawn script in bank 4 and sets $7F = 4 — the same format and the same interpreter as the labyrinth's, except that a wait counts frames in which $A0 bit 2 is set, which $E98F does when a new background row comes in. So waves are keyed to distance scrolled, not time. Command 7 ($E85E) loads the area's enemy art the same way the labyrinth does, from bank 4. Ground objects: each new row is 16 metatile ids in $04C0 ($E8AB); bank 5 $83B3 draws each from five bytes and writes the fifth back, and $89FB spawns an object for any cell whose fifth byte has a high nibble, from the lists bank 5 $803C names — so turrets and the like are placed in the scenery itself.

The checks. Corridors 1-21 name exactly one script each; areas n and n+10 share graphics streams, the same pairing the keys follow. The scripts and streams are pairwise disjoint, and all five scripts that end on a jump jump back into themselves. 139 of 144 (corridor, spawned type) pairs find the type's art block in that corridor's own load streams; the five that do not may be relying on art left loaded from before. Correction: the four huge “terminal triggers” that end bank 4's blocks are not trigger data — three are exactly the first two bytes of the spawn script or graphics stream that follows. Corridor 16's script runs on into the next block after its last wave; where it really ends is not established.

Loading enemy art

Enemy tiles are decompressed into CHR RAM as a room is entered. A load stream is [flags | slot][block][tile] records, bit 7 ending it. Bank 7 $E99F takes one record per pass: it evicts whatever was in slot (objects still using it become type $28), has $D7F9 decode block to tile tile — bank 3 below $40, bank 2 above — and records the block in $0480,slot and the tile in $0490,slot. An enemy whose block is not in $0480 waits ($CF5F); when it is, $0490 becomes its base tile. The check: in every stream, each record's tile is the previous one's plus that block's decoded length in tiles — the codec, the streams and the loader agree.

Labyrinth spawn lists: 3 pointers pointer_table lead

bank5.tbl_803C · bank 5 $803C-$8041 · 6 bytes

$89FB reads $803C,Y / $803D,Y with Y = 2 * $0478[low nibble of $04C0,X], then (pointer),Y with the high nibble for an object type. Three pointers, $AF61, $AF69, $AF71; the 6 bytes are exactly the gap between the entry table and the code at $8042. How far each list runs is NOT established - the index can reach 15 and the lists are 8 apart.

Layout step directions: -15, 1, 16, 17 data confirmed

bank5.tbl_82D9 · bank 5 $82D9-$82DC · 4 bytes

$82B9 LDA $82D9,Y with Y = the top two bits of a layout item: the step $82A3 adds between the six cells of its mask in the 16-wide room buffer - up-right, right, down, down-right. The BNE / BEQ pair at $82D5 jumps over it.

Enemy graphics: the default load stream data confirmed

bank5.data_A497 · bank 5 $A497-$A4C6 · 48 bytes

Sixteen [flags | slot][block][tile] records - $A46E points $28/$29 here with $27 = $80 on entering a room, and $E99F loads one block per pass into CHR at tile * 16, recording it in $0480/$0490. Bit 7 of the last record's first byte ($8F) ends it. THE CHECK: each record's tile is the previous one's plus that block's decoded tile count, all 15 pairs, $80 to $E2 + 14.

Spawn script pointers: 47 pointer_table confirmed

bank5.tbl_A4C7 · bank 5 $A4C7-$A524 · 94 bytes

$A480: LDA $A4C5,Y / $A4C6,Y with Y = 2 * $57, the script id from the map record; $57 = 0 skips it, so entry 0 is never read and the table starts at $A4C7. 47 entries, ending where the first target, $A525, begins - and the map uses ids 1-47, every one.

Enemy spawn scripts data confirmed

bank5.data_A525 · bank 5 $A525-$A662 · 318 bytes

The scripts bank 7 $F78F runs: < 3 a command (0 wait, 1 jump, 2 end, via the inline table at $F7C9), else a spawn - bit 7 clear one object of that type, bit 7 set a formation [type|$80][count][interval] carried by a type-$29 spawner. A spawn is followed by another bit-7 spawn or a wait in units of 60 frames. THE CHECK: walked from the 47 pointers they cover this stretch byte for byte. NOT ESTABLISHED: five scripts ($A58D, $A5BF, $A5D6, $A5F4, $A61F) end [byte] 01 02, which the code reads as a long wait and then a jump whose operand overlaps the next script. tools/parse-enemies.py --scripts decodes them all.

Miniboss rooms: sub-id to record data confirmed

bank5.tbl_A68D · bank 5 $A68D-$A6A2 · 22 bytes

$A66B: LDY $5E / LDA $A682,Y, for rooms of kind $40 - and $A682 itself is code, the STA $27 two instructions on, so sub-ids 0-10 could not be used. The sub-ids those rooms carry run 11-32, so the bytes read are $A68D-$A6A2 - starting exactly after the code, ending exactly before the records. Values are offsets 0-36 in steps of 3.

Miniboss rooms: 13 x [type][stream] data confirmed

bank5.tbl_A6A3 · bank 5 $A6A3-$A6C9 · 39 bytes

$A671-$A67D: the first byte to $72, the next two to $28/$29 as a graphics-load stream, then $27 = $80 starts the load. Types: $1D, $1E, $1F, $55, $56, $57, $58, $47, $5A, $5B, $5C, $5D, $5E. $72 is the boss type: $A663 also sets $70 = 1, the boss phase bank 3 $9184 runs for corridors too, which spawns type $72 ($92E5) and waits for it ($92EE) - so these are the labyrinth's minibosses, set out only while the room's sub-id flag is clear (JSR $C0E1). CORRECTION: named 'special rooms' with $72's use not established; see docs/labyrinth.html#minibosses.

bank5.data_A6CA · bank 5 $A6CA-$A6EA · 33 bytes

Seven streams in the same [flags | slot][block][tile] format, named by the records at $A6A3. They tile this stretch exactly and end on the code at $A6EB; the tile positions inside them pack block by block like the default stream's.

Hitbox half-width, by metasprite id data confirmed

bank7.tbl_C174 · bank 7 $C174-$C200 · 141 bytes

$D229: $0530 +/- $C174,Y into $06F8/$06E0, Y = the metasprite id. 141 bytes, one per metasprite id - bounded by $C201, read by the same routine.

Hitbox half-height, by metasprite id data confirmed

bank7.tbl_C201 · bank 7 $C201-$C28C · 140 bytes

$D229: LDA $0548,X (the metasprite id) / TAY, then $0518 +/- $C201,Y into $0728/$0710 - the vertical extent $D364 overlaps. 140 bytes, ending where the metasprite pointer table begins; id 140 would read its first byte.

The tile block holding each type's art data confirmed

bank7.tbl_CFC4 · bank 7 $CFC4-$D02B · 104 bytes

$CF4C: type AND $7F, CMP #$0E / BCC returns 0, else LDA $CFB6,Y - so this table starts at type $0E, and it runs to $D02B, type $75. A negative entry means 'per object' ($07B8,X). $CF5F finds the id in the loaded list $0480 and makes the object wait until it is there; $0490 then gives the tile the block was loaded at. THE CHECK: all 52 distinct ids name a real tile block when routed the way $EA58 routes them (below $40 bank 3, else bank 2 id - $30).

Enemy collision flags, by type data confirmed

bank7.tbl_D02C · bank 7 $D02C-$D0AA · 127 bytes

$CFA0 copies it into the slot with LDA table,Y where Y = type AND $7F - four reads six bytes apart, which is also what bounds the tables. Destination $0578. $D348 skips an object whose bit 7 is set and ANDs the rest with the collision class it is testing ($30 or $20). 127 bytes, types 0-126: type $7F would read $D0AB's first byte.

Enemy hit points, by type data confirmed

bank7.tbl_D0AB · bank 7 $D0AB-$D129 · 127 bytes

$CFA0 copies it into the slot with LDA table,Y where Y = type AND $7F - four reads six bytes apart, which is also what bounds the tables. Destination $0590, HIT POINTS: $D30E subtracts the other side's $05A8 from it, clamping at 0, and $D32A turns the object into its death type when it reaches 0. Families climb in step - types $10-$13 have 24, 32, 48, 80.

Enemy attack, by type data confirmed

bank7.tbl_D12A · bank 7 $D12A-$D1A8 · 127 bytes

$CFA0 copies it into the slot with LDA table,Y where Y = type AND $7F - four reads six bytes apart, which is also what bounds the tables. Destination $05A8, ATTACK: the hit points an object takes from whatever it collides with ($D30E). For the player the damage is divided by the player's own $0590 first ($D2DC-$D2DF, through $F9AE).

Per-type value copied to $0620 data confirmed

bank7.tbl_D1A9 · bank 7 $D1A9-$D228 · 128 bytes

$CFA0 copies it into the slot with LDA table,Y where Y = type AND $7F - four reads six bytes apart, which is also what bounds the tables. Destination $0620: DRAWING FLAGS. The draw path $CBE8 tests them bit by bit - bit 0 calls $CC88 and bit 1 $CCEB before drawing, bit 2 flips the attribute when $05D8 is non-negative, bit 3 is tested at $CC1F - so the per-type value says how the object is drawn. What each extra step does is not yet read. 128 bytes, ending at the code at $D229.

What each type becomes at 0 HP data confirmed

bank7.tbl_D441 · bank 7 $D441-$D4C0 · 128 bytes

$D32A: when $0590 reaches 0, LDA $D441,Y / STA $0500,X with Y = the type, after saving the old type in $0740. Mostly $08 and $07 - explosions. $D2F3 reads $D442 directly for the player (type 1). 128 bytes, ending at the code at $D4C1.

Score class, by type data confirmed

bank7.tbl_E00D · bank 7 $E00D-$E08C · 128 bytes

$DFB1: LDY $0740,X (the dead object's type, saved by $D32A) / LDA $E00D,Y; negative means per object, from $07D0,X. $DFCF turns the class into six decimal digits at $E08C + 6 x class + 1 and adds them into the score at $0170-$0175, capping at 999999. Classes 0-17 occur, plus $FF. 128 entries: type 127's is the byte at $E08C, which is also the never-read first byte of the digit rows (class 0's digits start at $E08D) - the overlap trick the split tables use. Values: class 0 = 0, class 1 = 1, class 2 = 6, class 3 = 10, class 4 = 17, class 5 = 20, class 6 = 30, class 7 = 50, class 8 = 80, class 9 = 100, class 10 = 200, class 11 = 400, class 12 = 800, class 13 = 1000, class 14 = 1500, class 15 = 2000, class 16 = 3000, class 17 = 4000.

Score values: 18 classes x 6 digits data confirmed

bank7.tbl_E08D · bank 7 $E08D-$E0F8 · 108 bytes

Six decimal digits per class, most significant first, read by $DFE3 LDA $E08C,Y with Y counting down from 6 x class + 6. The highest class any type names is 17, and 18 x 6 bytes from $E08D end exactly at $E0F8, where the code resumes.
